lessons.title: Retrieve, check, and plan the next session
lessons.objective: Perform a brief closed-reference retrieval attempt, compare it with a source, record a specific correction, and plan a feasible spaced return with a concrete task and fallback.
scope: Specific time/trigger, duration, deliverable and fallback
Adapt spacing to observed recall; no universal schedule or score
examples: Replace rereading with a two-question recall attempt
Use a missed unit conversion to select review
Fit a 25-minute session and a later return
Recover a missed session without abandoning the plan
lessons.guided: Write a recall prompt, an attempted answer, a specific correction and a feasible next visit from a supplied short topic.
lessons.activity: Seeded retrieval-planning worksheet with closed-reference instruction and attempt/correction fields; self-checked completion records the cycle rather than a mastery score.
fields: Next session: trigger, duration, and task
Fallback and evidence to check next time
rubric: attempt
I attempted recall before checking a reference and kept what I actually recalled.
feedback
I checked against a source and named a specific correction or verified detail.
return
My next session has a feasible trigger, task, duration, and fallback.

diagnostic.prompt: A worked example feels familiar, but you cannot explain its first step with the page closed. What should you do next?
options: retrieve
Attempt a small recall prompt, check it, and target the gap
An unaided attempt makes the missing step visible and gives feedback a purpose.
familiar
Count the familiar feeling as independent evidence
Recognition while reading does not show that you can retrieve or apply the reasoning.
repeat
Only reread until every sentence looks familiar
Rereading can clarify content, but it does not replace trying to produce the reasoning.

mistakes: Name a small deliverable and return trigger.
Preserve the unaided attempt before comparison.
Missed session treated as failure of the entire plan
Use a smaller fallback and reschedule the next concrete step.

lessons.title: Read technical text and decode notation
lessons.objective: Extract a technical passage's claim and conditions, define its symbols and units, translate its notation into a small checked example, and record a precise unresolved question.
scope: Preview and question before dense reading
Equality versus approximation, subscripts, function notation and units
Paraphrase, small-example check and precise question
examples: Read a constant-rate model without dropping its condition
Distinguish v₀ from v multiplied by zero
Turn f(x) into an input-output statement
Summarize a rounding claim with ≈ instead of =
lessons.guided: Read an original short storage-rate passage, create a symbol key, test a numerical example and state an excluded cost.
lessons.activity: Three seeded original technical passages: rate model, affine function and sampling interval. Learner produces claim, notation, example and question.
fields: Main claim and conditions in your own words
A small example and its check
Precise question and where to look next
rubric: conditions
My paraphrase keeps the assumptions and allowed inputs.
notation
I defined symbols and units without confusing labels with operations.
example
I checked an example and stated a specific remaining question.

diagnostic.prompt: A passage says d = vt for constant speed v. Your notes keep the equation but omit 'constant speed.' What is missing?
options: condition
A condition that limits when the model applies
The equation's meaning depends on its stated model conditions.
nothing
Nothing; the equation applies to every motion
A formula without its conditions can be used outside its scope.
font
Only a formatting detail
The phrase constrains the model rather than its appearance.

mistakes: Write one claim, its conditions and one example.
Consult the definition before manipulating a symbol.
Keep the allowed inputs and assumptions beside the relationship.

lessons.title: Check calculator settings and expression entry
lessons.objective: Predict a benchmark result, match degree or radian mode to the input, enter grouping and scientific notation explicitly, and explain discrepancies before trusting displayed digits.
scope: Known-angle checks in degrees and radians
Parentheses, unary minus and power grouping
Inverse function versus reciprocal; device syntax differs
examples: Compare -3² and (-3)² and group a denominator
Read 2.5e-3 and distinguish inverse sine from reciprocal
lessons.guided: Predict a half-unit sine benchmark, verify it in matching modes, then compare two expressions that differ only in grouping.
lessons.activity: Keyboard-accessible bounded calculator lab: degree/radian setting, predefined numeric inputs including π fractions, sine/cosine/inverse-sine, explicit grouping/scientific-notation cases, required prediction, immediate explanatory feedback and reset on changes. Local practice never writes completion.
fields: Tool result and expression actually entered
rubric: settings
I matched the angle unit and settings or stated why angle mode is irrelevant.
entry
I recorded explicit grouping and notation rather than only a display value.
check
I compared the result with a benchmark and explained any discrepancy.

diagnostic.prompt: A calculator gives about -0.988 for sin(30), while you expected 0.5 for 30°. What is the first useful check?
options: mode
Check whether the input was interpreted in radians
Thirty radians and thirty degrees are different angles.
round
Round the displayed value to 0.5
Rounding cannot explain this discrepancy.
trust
Accept the display because it has many digits
Digits do not establish that the intended quantity was entered.

mistakes: Use a known benchmark before the main calculation.
Write the exact intended expression with parentheses.
Scientific e mistaken for Euler's number
Read e-3 in the stated calculator convention as times ten to minus three.
Read the function name and check its input/output meaning.

lessons.title: Organize files and verify a recoverable copy
lessons.objective: Choose a descriptive file and revision scheme, save and reopen a harmless practice artifact, compare its contents with an expected marker, and explain how app progress exports and restores affect saved work.
scope: Filename, folder, extension and revision purpose
Local browser progress, export, import review and replacement
Independent copies and safe restore rehearsal; no forced reset or external account
examples: Replace final-final names with a descriptive revision
Reopen a practice artifact and compare a marker
Review a dated progress export before replacing newer work
Preserve a malformed or older file and locate a readable copy
lessons.guided: Prepare a file naming rule, use the local sample round-trip tool and record exactly what was reopened and verified.
lessons.activity: Local-only synthetic JSON round-trip: draft a short marker note, download a clearly labeled practice file, select it again, validate its small strict schema and compare exact marker/revision/content. Invalid/wrong files get targeted feedback. This is separate from real progress exports; link existing Settings for actual backup and import review.
fields: Folder, descriptive filename, and revision rule
Saved file and observed reopen check
rubric: file
I saved and reopened the harmless practice file and compared its marker and contents.
versions
My naming rule distinguishes purpose, revision, and file type.
restore
I explained backup verification and replacement without discarding newer work.

diagnostic.prompt: You downloaded a progress backup last month, then added newer notes. What should happen before importing the old file as a replacement?
options: review
Export current work, inspect the chosen backup, and review what replacement means
A readable older backup can still omit newer work; replacement is not a merge.
replace
Replace immediately because any backup is current
The file's date and contents matter.
rename
Rename the old file with today's date and import it
Renaming does not update the file's contents.

mistakes: Compare a known content marker after reopening.
Two copies only on one device
Plan another suitable location for an independent copy.
Export current work and review the replacement summary first.
Extension renamed to convert a file
Use the appropriate export; keep the extension matching actual content.
